summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and known coronary artery disease with prior stents presented after awakening with 20 minutes of chest pain and diaphoresis radiating to both arms. He took aspirin and was transported by EMS. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no acute EKG changes, and troponin levels below his baseline, ruling out a heart attack. Mild hyperkalemia and leukocytosis were noted, with the former corrected by inpatient hemodialysis and the latter resolving spontaneously without signs of infection. A chest X-ray showed mild congestive heart failure with interstitial opacities and mild cardiomegaly. The patient remained chest pain-free during admission, and no changes were made to his cardiac medications. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his cardiologist and continue all home therapies, including dialysis.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
